worktree: Freebuff cloud workspace; cloud-only, no dependency on the owner laptop
objective: Prepare the alternative real worker chain FAHAD OFFICE -> OPENCODE -> GEMINI CLI for Phase N on the VPS: verify official CLI interfaces, upgrade the OpenCode adapter, build a Gemini CLI adapter, keep the shared driver and a vendor-neutral failure taxonomy, register the workers truthfully, ship a VPS setup script and auth runbook, build the real Phase N drill command with restart/recovery and fail-closed termination proof, run targeted tests, and document without touching production.
decisions: Both new workers are real adapters built only against verified official interfaces: OpenCode (opencode run --format json, stdin prompt, --session resume, --auto, auth list) from the official docs and published run command source; Gemini CLI (non-TTY headless, --output-format stream-json, --approval-mode yolo, --skip-trust, init.session_id/result.stats, exit codes 0/1/41/42/53) from docs/cli/headless.md and the installed official 0.40.1 package. No guessed flags.

Gemini CLI declares resume:false because --resume only accepts "latest" or a numeric index; neither is a durable id and "latest" could resume another task's session, so recovery always starts a fresh session from the continuation packet at the exact checkpoint commit (supervisor falls back to start()).

Both adapters are OFF by default and share one env wiring point (externalAdaptersFromEnv in src/continuity/runtime.js) used by the production runtime and the drill, so drill wiring cannot drift from production.

The failure taxonomy is formalized as FAILURE_TAXONOMY/failureCategory() in src/continuity/errors.js: eight distinguishable categories (AUTH_REQUIRED, UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE, HOST_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED, RATE_LIMITED, PROCESS_FAILED, STOP_UNCONFIRMED, WORKTREE_UNSAFE) mapped onto the unchanged runtime codes; readiness states win over run-time codes when both are present.

The worker registry grows from seven to eight with a NEW data-only migration (20261005090000, insert disabled gemini-cli row, on conflict do nothing): the Phase A migration is never edited, no schema object changes, and the replayed fingerprint content matches supabase/verify/schema-fingerprint.txt exactly, so that file is untouched.

The live drill keeps production fully out of scope: disposable branch, disposable worktrees and an isolated file-persisted Continuity store; production Supabase continuity tables remain unapplied and only the Office worker's own documented agent_sessions interface is used.

Restart/recovery in the drill is fail-closed by construction: the first recovery attempt after a real SIGKILL is deliberately refused (no sealed termination proof), then the OS-verified proof is sealed and only the second attempt may reclaim the lease and resume from the exact commit.
OpenCode's four Zen gates plus auto-reload-off became explicit owner assertions via environment flags, all default closed; production flags remain untouched.

summary_md: Alternative-workers VPS preparation sprint: the OpenCode adapter is now a real executable adapter and a new Gemini CLI adapter was built, both only against verified official interfaces, both OFF by default and wired through one shared env factory. The failure taxonomy is formalized into eight distinguishable categories, the registry gains a data-only disabled gemini-cli row (fingerprint unchanged), and this branch ships ops/setup-continuity-workers.sh (--check/--install), docs/CONTINUITY-VPS-WORKERS.md (install, auth, flags, taxonomy, drill, rollback, status) and tools/continuity-phase-n-live.mjs (real chain evidence plus fail-closed restart/recovery). Targeted tests: focused continuity 75/75, docs and Hermes suites green, db:replay 33 migrations with all scenarios, fingerprint content identical, drill selftest green, drill --check refuses this unauthenticated environment with exact blockers. Verdict: ALTERNATIVE WORKERS PREPARED - READY FOR VPS LIVE PHASE N. Production untouched.
